tasks.short: Coordinate work with other project activities

steps.what: Discuss current work and constraints with other construction activity leads
Coordinate work activities and agree workable interfaces with other project leads

tasks.design: Keep cross-activity discussions and interface decisions with the supervisor and other leads. An existing {PROJECT} programme may inform them, but no separate repetitive scheduling activity is counted again here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination depends on live constraints and agreements between responsible people.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared programme supports discussion without resolving contextual conflicts itself.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting access needs and work that changes during the day.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating a workable interface and recognising when agreement is unsafe or incomplete.

reach.task: Resolve conflicts that exceed the supervisor's scope
reach.learn: Which interfaces need a project-level decision

evidence.claim: Live cross-activity coordination remains human work in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is cross-activity coordination, excluding activity-schedule rewriting counted under scheduling.
s1 produces understood conflicts through retained discussion; no free structured dependency feed is assumed.
Other leads' existing discussion time is unchanged and is not credited as a focal-role saving.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Conflict frequency and existing coordination routines
research_questions: Is there separately measured duplicate status reporting outside these necessary discussions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100. Discussion and agreement time remains unchanged with zero incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess job conditions and capture quantities material allowances and worker productivity assumptions
Calculate and assemble material and worker requirements estimate tables
Review estimate against job conditions and adjust assumptions before sharing requirements

tasks.design: Configure calculation and output templates in {SPREADSHEET} or an existing estimating module before building code. Generate the estimate tables from the supervisor's checked quantities and chosen productivity assumptions; retain takeoff, site judgement and final review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual calculations and table assembly sit between site assessment and estimate review.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic templates can calculate quantities and labour from explicit assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain ground conditions, waste and achievable productivity.
tasks.human_edge: Selecting defensible assumptions for the actual job rather than trusting a standard rate blindly.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and table assembly; the supervisor still owns the estimate assumptions.

reach.task: Compare site assumptions with measured completed-job quantities
reach.learn: Which rate adjustments reflect real conditions

evidence.claim: Deterministic estimate tables can use explicit quantities, units and rates without automating site judgement; the time split is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is a requirements estimate, excluding technical design and procurement commitment.
s1 counts takeoff and structured capture of work item, quantity, unit, material coefficient, waste allowance, selected labour rate, rate unit and scope revision; the supervisor is the producer.
The supervisor selects and records rate assumptions in s1; existing references are inputs, not an assumed ready-made estimate.
s2 only applies explicit arithmetic and assembles tables. Missing rates or mismatched units stop generation for manual correction in retained s1/s3.
Test native templates first. Savings apply only where arithmetic/table assembly is actually manual; existing formula runtime is excluded.
s3 retains full reasonableness review and corrections; repeated recalculation does not replace reassessing assumptions.
unknowns: Actual manual calculation share and existing template coverage
research_questions: Does the template remove table assembly while preserving takeoff and assumption-review time?

already_counted.description: Estimate input capture and final reasonableness review

incremental.description: Maintain calculation templates and compare rate revisions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+0+25=75; gross 25 minus 1 upkeep gives central net 24. High requires genuinely manual calculation/table assembly; low covers existing automation or difficult jobs absorbing the benefit in corrections.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Investigate worker or production problems through observation and discussion
Analyze causes and recommend production method improvements or appropriate worker support

tasks.design: Keep investigation and recommendations with the supervisor and affected people. {DOCS} can retain existing procedures, but a generated diagnosis or worker score is not introduced as a substitute for understanding the problem.
tasks.previous_blocker: Causes mix physical constraints, methods and people.
tasks.enabler_now: No reliable structured causal input has been established.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing individual difficulty from unsafe methods or poor planning.
tasks.human_edge: Building enough trust for workers to explain what is going wrong.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a proposed method change is practical for the crew
reach.learn: How to test a change without blaming workers

evidence.claim: The design retains contextual diagnosis and worker discussions, without a claimed software saving.

assumptions: Boundary is investigation and recommendation, excluding implementation of a changed method.
s1 produces the problem context through retained observations and discussion; no structured cause or motivation flag is assumed.
No new worker ranking, monitoring feed or model diagnosis is introduced.
No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Problem mix and local improvement practices
research_questions: Is recurring evidence collation a real separate burden rather than necessary investigation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100. Investigation and recommendations retain full time with no incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check site needs quantities specifications and delivery constraints for materials
Prepare materials order or requisition with supplier and delivery details
Check exact requisition and approve submission within purchasing authority

tasks.design: Configure reusable catalogue lines and delivery defaults in {PROCUREMENT} to prepare a draft from checked needs. The supervisor checks the complete version before submitting a requisition; supplier commitment continues through the existing authorised purchasing route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated entry of catalogue, supplier and delivery information slows requisitions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native purchase forms can reuse approved fields without selecting substitutes autonomously.
tasks.still_hard: Changed site needs, unavailable materials and technically unsuitable substitutions.
tasks.human_edge: Checking that the item and delivery arrangement fit actual work.
tasks.altitude: Less order preparation; purchasing limits and material judgement stay unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve unavailable catalogue materials and supplier terms

evidence.claim: Native catalogue-based order preparation is a plausible deterministic design; this digest does not directly establish its deployment or saving for this task.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the supervisor's authorised requisition submission; purchasing approval, supplier fulfilment and receiving are unchanged outside it.
The supervisor produces item specification, quantity, unit, job, needed date and actual delivery location in s1; all inspection and capture time remains counted.
The existing buyer-maintained catalogue supplies item code, supplier, price, unit and terms through unchanged procurement work; additional catalogue corrections have a separate upkeep allowance.
s2 retains item matching, input entry and missing-data fallback. No structured address or sold-out flag is assumed without a producer.
Test native favourites and defaults first; missing catalogue data or substitutes require manual buyer resolution through the current route.
s3 binds submission to the exact draft version; any change invalidates approval. The tool adds no authority to commit the supplier.
unknowns: Native catalogue coverage and supervisor purchasing authority
research_questions: Can repeat lines be reused without increasing buyer corrections or reducing specification checks?

already_counted.description: Draft matching and exceptions in s2
Full requisition check and submission approval in s3

incremental.description: Maintain local defaults and inspect failed repeat lines

approvals.approved_version: Exact job, item codes/specifications, quantities, units, supplier, prices, delivery location/date and requisition version; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+10.5+25=75.5; gross 24.5 minus 1 focal upkeep gives net 23.5. High needs repeated catalogue items; low covers unusual specifications or missing defaults. Buyer upkeep remains separately visible.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce estimate assembly and requisition rekeying while retaining site judgement and people leadership.
reach: Work with estimators and buyers using explicit assumptions and specifications
role.ambitious_version: Give project colleagues clear estimates and requisitions while keeping construction decisions accountable.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
